paper.title_en: Effect of fluid anisotropy on self-gravitating compact objects: A comparative study of Einstein’s and non-conserved gravity
paper.abstract_en:
We formulate a novel class of interior solutions in this study that describe anisotropic compact objects under
Rastall theory. The assumption of a spherically symmetric matter distribution is made in this context to start
off our analysis, along with specific forms of anisotropy, which are useful for finding the exact solutions of
the non-conserved field equations. Using the provided radial metric functions, we attain differential equations
in relation to the temporal component. These equations are then integrated to determine the corresponding
function containing multiple constants. The interior solutions are matched with the vacuum exterior metric
at the hypersurface of a compact star to find out these constants. To introduce the Rastall parameter in these
constants, the requirement of zero pressure in the radial direction at the spherical edge is also applied. Later
on, we analyze substantial properties and key stability criteria for the developed models. The observed data
from two compact stars, i.e., LMC X-4 and 4U 1820-30 is utilized to carry out the graphical evaluation. We
conclude our models to be strongly aligned with the necessary criteria that ensures their physical existence
for certain choices of the Rastall parameter that governs the matter–geometry coupling.
